fields.question: Why is pointwise relevance insufficient?
fields.answer: A set must cover complementary information and avoid any harmful evidence; individually relevant documents need not form a useful set.
fields.example: Teaching example: separate price/performance documents can cover positive criteria collectively, but either document can trigger an outdated-price penalty.

fields.question: What does a poor rollout imitate?
fields.answer: It maximizes the best in-group trajectory likelihood, weighted by its reward gap, rather than imitating its own failure.
fields.example: Teaching example: with rewards0,1,3, the first two imitate the reward3 token sequence with weights3 and2.

fields.question: Does Yuanbao change the same layer as WeSearch?
fields.answer: No. It aligns utility supervision and subset selection; WeSearch primarily changes atomic matching within cluster-constrained candidates.
fields.example: Teaching example: correct ADC distances do not prove a final evidence set is nonredundant, complete or current.

fields.question: What happens when all rewards tie?
fields.answer: Advantages and best-reward gaps are zero, so neither branch fabricates a policy update; padding must still receive no gradient.
fields.example: Teaching example: rewards all equal to2 yield zero update; arbitrarily small padding log probabilities must not change the loss.

fields.question: Why does ABA not retrain the encoder?
fields.answer: It corrects event logits after fixing the predictor; CPC/RW handle representation learning, keeping calibration separate.
fields.example: Teaching example: a promotion peak changes the ABA event amplitude without retraining the historical encoder.

fields.question: Do CPC and RW share the same gradient convention?
fields.answer: No. CPC eta participates in backpropagation; RW omega is detached and only scales supervised gradients. Detaching both changes the algorithm.
fields.example: Teaching example: identical views give a CPC gate of0.5; an RW distance below the mean can receive a weight above1.

fields.question: Can COTTI replace BAFF interference handling?
fields.answer: No. Historical distance is not counterfactual exposure/interference evidence; promotion calibration and polluted experiment logs are different problems.
fields.example: Teaching example: online HDR and offline TEN are different controls, not interchangeable causal baselines.

fields.question: Why can ABA worsen calibration?
fields.answer: A nonnegative event amplitude times tanh variance only raises probabilities. Already-overpredicted groups can worsen, requiring separate subgroup calibration and novel-category recall analysis.
fields.example: Teaching example: an overpredicted0.8 probability is still raised by nonnegative ABA; retain this adverse result.

fields.question: Why can one watch image yield different relevance labels?
fields.answer: Exact-model search requires entity correspondence, while strap-durability questions can accept transferable material/use evidence from another model.
fields.example: Teaching example: one candidate can be grade0/1 for an exact-model request but grade2 for a transferable leather-strap durability question.

fields.question: Are residual experts six independent query encoders?
fields.answer: No. Each branch shares a down bottleneck and mixes six up projections with one query gate, preserving the base projection and document space.
fields.example: Teaching example: rank8/64 branches each share a down matrix; their gate is not a hand-written intent one-hot.

fields.question: How does it differ from WeSearch cluster constraints?
fields.answer: Fixed-index adaptation changes how a query maps into existing document space; cluster constraints organize candidates. They can combine but are not substitutes.
fields.example: Teaching example: changing query residuals with bitwise-unchanged documents proves only the fixed-index interface.

fields.question: May the CSLS reference bank use test queries?
fields.answer: Do not tune on test distribution or labels. The paper uses training queries to precompute document density for the adapted model; serving only adjusts candidate scores.
fields.example: Teaching example: a document with high training-query similarity receives a larger density correction; do not choose k using test hit rates.

fields.question: How many SIMQ+ hits arise when one query token reaches three clusters of one document?
fields.answer: One. Counts measure distinct query-token coverage, not cluster multiplicity.
fields.example: Teaching example: three clusters containingdocA add only one hit for that token.

fields.question: Why can SIMQ+ rerank more thanNmin documents?
fields.answer: It uses the largest integer count threshold retaining at leastNmin and keeps every boundary tie.
fields.example: Teaching example: if ranks4–6 tie withNmin=4, all six remain.

fields.question: Can SIMQ replace HVMap heterogeneous-space alignment?
fields.answer: No. SIMQ changes candidate indexing within one token space; HVMap learns cross-space mappings.
fields.example: Teaching example: equal vector dimensionality does not make two encoders comparable by SIMQ inner products.

fields.question: Does a working exact local build establish CPU throughput gains?
fields.answer: No. It is a small-data backend with real traversal/reranking, not scalable HNSW or matched-recall QPS measurement.
fields.example: Teaching example: correct counts on12 documents do not predict million-document latency.

fields.question: Why can a fixed-alpha graph fail another query?
fields.answer: Alpha changes hybrid order and neighborhoods; a0.5 graph can miss lexical- or semantic-dominant neighbors.
fields.example: Teaching example: movingalpha from0.3 to0.7 can change the useful entry point.

fields.question: Is stronger pruning at smaller gamma still safe?
fields.answer: Not guaranteed. Onlygamma=1 directly yields the Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound; smaller values add a positive margin and can discard useful vertices.
fields.example: Teaching example: fewer sparse dot products may cost recall.

fields.question: Is UniGraph alpha the HVMap native weight?
fields.answer: No. It mixes dense/sparse distances, whereas HVMap weights native/mapped scores.
fields.example: Teaching example: raisingalpha does not mean trusting a candidate’s own database more.

fields.question: Does matching unpruned beam search atgamma1 prove exact retrieval?
fields.answer: No. It preserves that beam’s insertion decisions, while graph reachability, entries and finite beam still limit recall.
fields.example: Teaching example: a never-visited true neighbor is not recovered merely by a safe bound.

fields.question: Why can a better retriever suffer more from contiguous chunks?
fields.answer: Strong documents concentrate in the prefix and exceed one chunk’s quota.
fields.example: Teaching example: twenty good prefix documents with quota4 lose sixteen when crowded together; dealing spreads them.

fields.question: Do six calls/two rounds guarantee the full top10?
fields.answer: No. The consistent-ranker proposition guarantees topq, hereq=4; the other six depend on expected-cut analysis.
fields.example: Teaching example: exact top4 does not imply lossless nDCG@10.

fields.question: Can it replace HVMap dual-space reranking?
fields.answer: No. DealRank determines which candidates share a comparison; HVMap defines comparable cross-encoder scores.
fields.example: Teaching example: dealing cannot align incompatible embeddings.

fields.question: What does a deterministic-ranker diagnostic establish?
fields.answer: Only concurrency, quota accounting and permutation conservation on controls, not LLM prompting or latency.
fields.example: Teaching example: an evaluator’s ranking table must not become a model-visible answer.

fields.question: Why is a November intake not a November first release?
fields.answer: The Google repository is new; arXivv1 is from March2. First-author grouping remains Michigan with Google collaboration separate.
fields.example: Teaching example: a November16 commit cannot replace the original arXiv date.

fields.question: Why freeze model/prompt factors during human calibration?
fields.answer: Autorater data learns shared features; scarce human labels fit an alignment head, and conditional inference treats those features as fixed.
fields.example: Teaching example: human loss must not update stage1 prompt vectors.

fields.question: Is it the same method as cost-saving ProEval?
fields.answer: No. ProEval actively selects target items and updates a GP, while this model calibrates raters to human judgments.
fields.example: Teaching example: adding a cheap judge label is not selecting a human evaluation item.

fields.question: May the same interval be used after all-parameter human fine-tuning?
fields.answer: No. It assumes fixed features and ignores stage1 estimation error. Fine-tuning changes that condition.
fields.example: Teaching example: supplying an identitySigma tests arithmetic, not real coverage.

fields.question: Why is a creative gene not just the final script?
fields.answer: It is a structured planning/production interface specifying narrative units and rules, followed by storyboards, clips, narration and rendering.
fields.example: Teaching example: a trust-building unit does not prove the rendered certification shot exists.

fields.question: Does a high LightGBM CTR-level mean real clicks?
fields.answer: No. It is a category-relative training surrogate; realCTR comes from production clicks/impressions.
fields.example: Teaching example: reward1 is not100%CTR.

fields.question: Is CutAgent memory the same as AgenticRecTune SkillHub?
fields.answer: Both reuse experience, but production-defect corrections conditioned on category/gene differ from recommendation-configuration experiments.
fields.example: Teaching example: avoiding repeated close-ups does not specify a recommendation fusion weight.

fields.question: Why must60.4% and2.21% remain separate?
fields.answer: The former is forced-choice human preference and the latter production clicks/impressions. Their denominators and objects differ; this round is review-only.
fields.example: Teaching example: a participant choosing a video is not an ad-slot click.
